title: Παῖς κλέπτης καὶ μήτηρ
titleEn: The Thieving Boy and His Mother
part: The Thieving Boy and His Mother (Chambry 296)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 296. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Παῖς ἐκ διδασκαλείου τὴν τοῦ συμφοιτητοῦ δέλτον ὑφελόμενος τῇ μητρὶ ἐκόμισε.
sentences.tr: Pais ek didaskaleiou tēn tou symphoitētou delton hyphelomenos tēi mētri ekomise.
sentences.l: A boy, having filched his fellow-pupil's tablet from the school, brought it to his mother.
sentences.n: δέλτος is the waxed writing-tablet a schoolboy carried; the first theft is small and domestic. ὑφαιρέομαι in the middle is to draw a thing away for oneself on the sly.

sentences.t: Τῆς δὲ οὐ μόνον αὐτῷ μὴ ἐπιπληξάσης, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον ἐπαινεσάσης αὐτόν, ἐκ δευτέρου ἱμάτιον κλέψας ἤνεγκεν αὐτῇ.
sentences.tr: Tēs de ou monon autōi mē epiplēxasēs, alla mallon epainesasēs auton, ek deuterou himation klepsas ēnenken autēi.
sentences.l: And when she not only did not rebuke him but rather praised him, a second time, having stolen a cloak, he brought it to her.
sentences.i: And since she not only did not rebuke him but actually praised him, the next time he stole a cloak and brought it to her.
sentences.n: A genitive absolute again, and it will carry most of this fable: each of the mother's failures to act is set down in that construction while the boy's doings take the main verbs. ἐπιπλήττω, 'strike at', takes the dative of the person rebuked.

sentences.t: Ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον ἐπαινεσάσης αὐτὸν ἐκείνης, προϊὼν τοῖς χρόνοις, ὡς νεανίας ἐγένετο, ἤδη καὶ τὰ μείζονα κλέπτειν ἐπεχείρει.
sentences.tr: Eti de mallon epainesasēs auton ekeinēs, proiōn tois chronois, hōs neanias egeneto, ēdē kai ta meizona kleptein epecheirei.
sentences.l: And when she praised him still more, he, going forward in years, when he became a young man, was by now attempting to steal greater things as well.
sentences.i: And when she praised him still more, then as the years went on and he came to be a young man, he was already trying his hand at bigger thefts.

sentences.t: Ληφθεὶς δέ ποτε ἐπ’ αὐτοφώρῳ καὶ περιαγκωνισθεὶς ἐπὶ τὸν δήμιον ἀπήγετο.
sentences.tr: Lēphtheis de pote ep’ autophōrōi kai periankōnistheis epi ton dēmion apēgeto.
sentences.l: But being caught one day in the very act, and having his arms pinioned behind him, he was being led off to the executioner.
sentences.n: ἐπ’ αὐτοφώρῳ is the legal phrase for a man taken in the theft itself, red-handed. περιαγκωνίζω is to bind the arms back behind the elbows. ὁ δήμιος, 'the public man', is the executioner.

sentences.t: Τῆς δὲ ἐπακολουθούσης αὐτῷ καὶ στερνοκοπουμένης, εἶπε βούλεσθαί τι αὐτῇ εἰπεῖν πρὸς τὸ οὖς· καὶ ἐπεὶ τάχιστα αὐτῷ προσῆλθε, τοῦ ὠτίου ἐπιλαβόμενος, κατέδακεν αὐτό.
sentences.tr: Tēs de epakolouthousēs autōi kai sternokopoumenēs, eipe boulesthai ti autēi eipein pros to ous· kai epei tachista autōi prosēlthe, tou ōtiou epilabomenos, katedaken auto.
sentences.l: And when she followed after him beating her breast, he said that he wished to say something to her in her ear; and as soon as she came up to him, taking hold of her ear, he bit it off.
sentences.n: στερνοκοπέομαι is to beat one's own breast, the formal gesture of mourning. ἐπεὶ τάχιστα is 'as soon as ever'. ἐπιλαμβάνομαι in the middle takes the genitive of what is taken hold of; ὠτίον is the diminutive of οὖς and means simply the ear. κατέδακεν is the strong compound, 'bit clean through'; the next sentence, with ἐλωβήσατο, confirms that the ear was maimed.

sentences.t: Τῆς δὲ κατηγορούσης αὐτοῦ δυσσέβειαν, εἴπερ μὴ ἀρκεσθεὶς οἷς ἤδη πεπλημμέληκε, καὶ τὴν μητέρα ἐλωβήσατο, ἐκεῖνος ὑποτυχὼν εἶπεν· « Ἀλλὰ τότε ὅτε σοι πρῶτον τὴν δέλτον κλέψας ἤνεγκα, εἰ ἐπέπληξάς μοι, οὐκ ἂν μέχρι τούτου ἐχώρησα, ὡς καὶ ἐπὶ θάνατον ἀπάγεσθαι. »
sentences.tr: Tēs de katēgorousēs autou dyssebeian, eiper mē arkestheis hois ēdē peplēmmelēke, kai tēn mētera elōbēsato, ekeinos hypotychōn eipen· « Alla tote hote soi prōton tēn delton klepsas ēnenka, ei epeplēxas moi, ouk an mechri toutou echōrēsa, hōs kai epi thanaton apagesthai. »
sentences.l: And when she charged him with impiety — seeing that, not content with the offences he had already committed, he had maimed his mother besides — he, taking-up-the-word, said: « But back then, when I first stole the tablet and brought it to you, if you had rebuked me, I would not have gone as far as this, so as even to be led away to death. »
sentences.i: And when she charged him with impiety, since he was not content with the wrongs he had already done but had maimed his own mother into the bargain, he answered: « But back then, when I first stole the tablet and brought it to you, if you had rebuked me, I would never have gone this far, to be led away to death. »
sentences.n: κατηγορέω takes the genitive of the person and the accusative of the charge. ἀρκέομαι, 'be content', takes the dative of what contents one — here οἷς, the wrongs already done. ὑποτυχών is the standing idiom for taking up the word in reply, not for any physical seizing. The retort is a past contrary-to-fact condition: aorist indicative in the if-clause, aorist indicative with ἄν in the conclusion — 'if you had rebuked me, I would not have gone'.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι τὸ κατ’ ἀρχὰς μὴ κολαζόμενον ἐπὶ μεῖζον αὔξεται.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti to kat’ archas mē kolazomenon epi meizon auxetai.
sentences.l: The story shows that what is not punished at the outset grows into something greater.
sentences.n: τὸ κατ’ ἀρχὰς μὴ κολαζόμενον is an articular participle doing the work of a noun, 'the thing not punished at the beginning'; the negative is μή rather than οὐ because the statement is general, not about one particular case.
